first: Ha, a new face! I am Pell. I left years ago; the roads brought me back.
A basket, a trowel, some food. And I buy what you find, at a fair price. Mostly.
Herbs for me, berries for Maru: help whoever you like first. I pay in coin.
stranger: Baskets, trowels, food. I buy what you find.
They say bells ring in the deep ruins at night. I charge extra after dark.
acquaintance: Herbs sell well. The best stand where the mist is thin at noon.
A glade lies west, past the old oak. The mist sits on it like a lid.
friend: Best customer this side of the river. Also the only one.
The garden behind the ruins was lovely once. Dark berries grew there, they say.

say: Sunleaf sells. I knew you had an eye. Or luck. Luck sells too.
